## Descripción
We received an encrypted message. The modulus is built from primes large enough that factoring them isn’t an option, at least not today. See if you can make sense of the numbers and reveal the flag. Download the [message](https://challenge-files.cylabacademy.net/library/c85258d1bfc43eacb36ad1dad1f13f53e3bb9de78790da47f98669733ded9001/message.txt).

Hints

1

When certain values in the encryption setup are smaller than usual, it opens up unexpected shortcuts to recover the plaintext

2

Consider whether you can invert the encryption without factoring `n`.

3

Read more about Coppersmith's_attack [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppersmith's_attack)
## Solución
```
Dark23-academy@webshell:~$ wget -O message.txt "https://challenge-files.cylabacademy.net/library/c85258d1bfc43eacb36ad1dad1f13f53e3bb9de78790da47f98669733ded9001/message.txt"


Dark23-academy@webshell:~$ cat message.txt
n = 
e = 20
c = 


Dark23-academy@webshell:~$ pip install pycryptodome gmpy2

Dark23-academy@webshell:~$ cat > solve.py << 'EOF'
> import re
> import gmpy2
> from Crypto.Util.number import long_to_bytes
> 
> txt = open("message.txt").read()
> vals = {}
> for name in ("n", "e", "c"):
>     m = re.search(rf"\b{name}\s*[=:]\s*(\d+)", txt, re.I)
>     vals[name] = int(m.group(1))
> n, e, c = vals["n"], vals["e"], vals["c"]
> print("e =", e)
> 
> for k in range(0, 1000000):
>     m, exact = gmpy2.iroot(c + k * n, e)
>     if exact:
>         print("k =", k)
>         print(long_to_bytes(int(m)).decode(errors="ignore"))
>         break
> else:
>     print("No encontrado")
> EOF
Dark23-academy@webshell:~$ python3 solve.py
e = 20
k = 0
academy{t1ny_e_d9b985d8}
```
